_comment: The dashboard's assembly, row by row (#155 R1, BOOTSTRAP.md §6): what the Period's stored rows add up to
for a Household on a given instant, and what the figures made of them are. trajectory.json takes aggregates
and so cannot pin the Period bounding, the day mapping, the folding of Expenses into them or the Daily Pool
through the Period; this file does.
`households` are seeded together into one database, and every `reads` row is answered for the Household
it sits in, so another Household's rows being present is part of every row (tenancy). `categories`,
`pockets` and `expenses` are keyed by `key` for the rows that name them; `active` defaults to true,
`deleted` to false, `allowance_mode` to adaptive. An Expense's currency is its Household's
`reporting_currency`. `captured_at` is set on some Expenses to a time that disagrees with `occurred_on` on
purpose: no figure reads it. `monthly_budgets` and `allocations` are the Budget's version logs by
`year_month` and `effective_on`; a Period marker is created for every `year_month` named here, and a
Period named by no row is brought into being by its first read, carrying forward the latest state of the
nearest earlier one (PRD S13).
A `reads` row: `now` is the instant of the request, the User's `time_zone` and the Household's
`day_starts_at` make Today of it, `period` is the Period containing Today, and `expected` is what the
assembly answers for it. `spend` is the daily bucket's spend in that Period: `by_day` (days with any),
`settled` before Today, `today`, `future` after Today up to the Period's last day. A Commitment Category's
Expense is in none of it, an uncategorised one is Daily, a deleted one is out, an inactive Category's or
Pocket's counts, a refund is negative, and an Expense dated outside the Period is in no figure of it.
`pool` is the Daily Pool as the target line is built from it: `today` (the one GET /budget answers as
`daily_pool` on the same state), `base` (as of the Period's first day: a Budget set on day 14 is its Budget
from day 1, versions dated before a re-cut window clamp to it and the latest wins) and `changes` (the days
after the first and on or before Today on which the pool really changed, with the pool from that day; a
version dated after Today is in no row, and a Daily Category's allocation, which leaves the pool alone, is
no change). `pace` is the State, Trajectory Variance and Buffer Days the calculation reads against the
target line, computed and pinned here for every row. It is absent exactly where the Household is fully
committed. `wire` is what `GET /dashboard` carries at this stage of #155: the currency, and the
`trajectory` once there is a Monthly Budget (with the D7 breakdowns, below). From PR 6 the trajectory
carries `state` and `trajectory_variance` from `pace`: both wherever `pace` is, except that on the Period's
first day (nothing has settled) `trajectory_variance` is absent and `state` reads afloat. Buffer Days is
never on the wire
(#155 R7). Each later PR adds its figures to every row here, so this file grows by assertions, not rows.
From PR 7 the `wire` of a row with a `trajectory` carries `categories` and `pockets` where they have rows
(#155 T10), written as the answer is but with a key for each id, since the ids are minted when the file is
seeded: `category` (a key of `categories`) in place of `category_id`, `pocket` in place of `pocket_id`; the
uncategorised row has no `category`. Both count the live Expenses dated in the Period and on or before Today,
the future-dated and the deleted left out; `categories` lists the daily bucket only (uncategorised spend as the
row with no `category`, a Commitment Category never) and `pockets` both buckets; `allocation` is the allocation
in force Today (the latest version dated on or before Today, as the Period's first Monthly Budget clamps it, or
the nearest earlier Period's latest state carried forward into a Period nobody had read), absent where there is
none; both lists are ordered by `spent` descending, and no row here ties, which would be the id's to break.
The breakdown rows were worked out the same way, by a script over this file's rows and these rules.
From PR 8 the `wire` of a row with a `trajectory` carries `chart.points` (#155 T8), one point for every day of
the Period: `target` is T(j), the cumulative target at the END of the day (the first point is one day's worth),
the target line of `pool` with every segment's slope clamped at zero, half-up at four decimals; `actual` is the
daily bucket's cumulative spend through that day (a Commitment's Expense never in it, uncategorised in it, a
refund subtracting), present up to and including Today and absent after; `in_progress` is true on Today's point
only. The points were worked out in exact Fractions from this file's raw Expenses and `pool`, not from the
`spend` block, and cross-checked against two figures this file pins on its own: the target on the day before
Today, less `spend.settled`, is the row's `trajectory_variance`, and Today's actual is `settled + today`.
A fully committed row's target is flat at zero (or at the value the line had reached), and its chart is there.
From PR 9 the `wire` of a row with a `trajectory` and a Commitment Category carries `commitments` (#155 T9,
R16): per Budget Period, `commitments_budget` the allocations in force Today (as `allocation` above, a
Period nobody had read carrying the nearest earlier one's latest state), `paid` the live Expenses of the
Commitment Categories dated in the Period and on or before Today (a future-dated one is not paid until its
day), `still_due` the difference, signed and never clamped (the first row: 3.000.000 paid against 2.500.000 is
-500.000), and `items`, one row for each live Commitment Category in the Category list's order, with `category`
in place of `category_id` as above. The rows were worked out the same way, by a script over this file's rows.
The last Household has two Commitment Categories, `rent` then `insurance` (the order they were made in, which
is neither alphabetical nor the order of what was paid), and carries the cases the first does not: an inactive
Commitment is a row and in the totals with its allocation in force; a zero allocation with nothing paid is a
row at 0.0000 throughout, and the allocation raised on the 10th is in force from then; a refund nets what was
paid; a deleted payment, one dated the day before the Period, one the day after it and one dated after Today
are in no `paid` (the last until its day: a payment dated Today is paid); `still_due` is zero when the
allocation is met. Its Commitment payments are in `pockets` (both buckets) and in no `categories` row.
Every expected value was worked out in exact rational arithmetic by a script that reads this file's
rows and CONTEXT.md's calculation spec, and not the backend: allowance figures floored at four decimals,
Variance and Buffer Days half-up, the State read from the exact Variance and baseline.

households.name: November, the first of the month, spend across every boundary

reads.name: Today is the 14th at exactly 04:00
one second earlier it is still the 13th, so the 13th's spend is Today's and the 14th's is future
the first day: nothing is settled
the last day: nothing is future
the Monthly Budget's day-11 change takes effect Today: the line kinks under Today, the slope in force is the new one
a Commitment's allocation changes Today (day 12): the pool moves with no Monthly Budget edit, and it kinks
the 20th: the cut that was after Today on the 14th is in force, and the line has three kinks
the next Period holds only what is dated in it

households.name: A Household that starts its Period on the 25th, in dollars, with no Monthly Budget and no Category

reads.name: the 26th, inside November's Period of the 25th
the 24th still belongs to October's Period

households.name: Re-cut to start on the 25th: Budget versions before, inside and after the window

reads.name: day 2: three versions and an allocation before the window, the latest of each is the base, and the day-3 version is after Today
day 3: a version inside the window takes effect Today
day 8: a Commitment's allocation inside the window kinks, a Daily Category's the day before did not, and the day-11 version is after Today
day 14: every version inside the window is in force, those before it are its base, and a future-dated Expense lowers the Available Pool
the last day: the version dated after the window's last day is in no figure

households.name: Fixed allowance mode, after a raise and then a cut below the target

reads.name: fixed mode after a raise: the allowance is the slope in force, not the flat one
fixed mode after a cut below the target: fully committed, so the allowance is 0 and there is no baseline, with money left

households.name: Commitments above the Monthly Budget, then a raise

reads.name: a negative Daily Pool from day 1: fully committed, so no baseline, and the allowance is negative as it is
the raise takes effect Today: the line starts from zero, not from where an unclamped line would have been
after the raise: the slope in force is the clamped one

households.name: A future-dated refund and an ordinary one

reads.name: the future-dated spend nets to a refund: the Available Pool is the whole pool, not raised by it; the refund dated the 4th has raised the allowance
the 26th: the refund and the spend are both past, so both are settled

households.name: A hot start: the warm-up pins afloat, then drifting, then taking on water

reads.name: two settled days: 2 days behind pace, but the warm-up pins the State to afloat
four settled days, one and a half days behind: drifting
nine settled days, three and a half days behind: taking on water

households.name: Two Commitments, one of them inactive: a refund, a deleted payment and a zero allocation

expenses.key: rent the day before the Period
insurance the day after the Period

reads.name: the 5th: the inactive Commitment has a zero allocation and nothing paid, and the deleted payment and the one dated the 8th are in no figure
the 20th: the refund nets the inactive Commitment's payment, which stays in the rows and the totals, and the 25th's rent is not paid yet
the 25th: a payment dated Today is paid, and the Commitments' rows keep the Category list's order, not the order of what was paid
